title: Unified token metering: input/output rate differentiation and streaming floor experiment
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Context: Our hosted API currently bills per-token without differentiating input vs output, and streaming usage is billed identically to non-streaming calls. Early enterprise feedback and telemetry indicate two pain points: 1) applications with long prompts (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation) create disproportionate input token volume that inflates cost for customers but has lower runtime cost for us, and 2) high-volume streaming applications (realtime assistants, live translation) create unpredictable invoice spikes and operational anomalies.

Goal: Design and validate an alternative metering model that separates input and output token rates and introduces a configurable streaming floor (minimum monthly streaming charge tier) to stabilize economics for both customers and Redwood. We want to measure commercial impact, product simplicity, and operational overhead.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Charging input tokens at a lower rate than output tokens will make RAG and long-context workloads more price-competitive and reduce churn for customers with heavy prompt usage.
- H2: Introducing a modest streaming floor (a predictable monthly minimum for streaming-enabled accounts) will reduce billing volatility and lower support incidents tied to unexpected spikes.
- H3: A combined IO split + streaming floor will increase ARPU by >6% on accounts using streaming features while improving retention for RAG-heavy customers by >3% over 90 days.

Why now: Pricing sensitivity surfaced in several enterprise security questionnaire reviews (customers asking about predictability and cost caps), and Dedicated/Private conversations repeatedly ask for clearer metering semantics. This experiment is a near-term lever that can be implemented in Hosted without infra changes to Dedicated/Private billing models initially.

Key artifacts: PRD: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/prd-hosted-pricing-experiments (internal), Design brief: https://docs.google.com/design/hosted-pricing-io-split, Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/hosted-pricing/iosplit-experiment, Draft contract language for enterprise security questionnaires: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SEC/Token+metering+language
acceptance_criteria: A1: Billing system emits separate input_token and output_token metrics and invoices reflect distinct rates for experiment cohorts
A2: Telemetry dashboards show cohort-level ARPU, churn, and support ticket volume; alerts configured for >10% unexpected delta
A3: Streaming floor config is plumbed into rate engine with ability to opt-in for customer segments and to set monthly minimums
A4: Legal/Contracts team reviews and signs off on updated security questionnaire language regarding metering and data retention
A5: Experiment runs for at least 4 weeks with statistically significant signals for primary metrics or clear stop conditions
metrics: Primary: delta ARPU (cohort vs control) over 30/60/90 days
Secondary: 90-day retention delta for RAG-heavy customers (>50% input tokens), support ticket rate per 1k accounts, average invoice volatility (stddev monthly spend)
Operational: billing repro rate, invoice disputes count, latency of invoice generation pipeline
approach: Design 2x treatment variants: (T1) IO split where input tokens billed at 0.6x base rate and output tokens at 1.0x base rate; (T2) IO split + streaming floor (monthly minimum $50 for streaming-enabled accounts)
Select experiment cohorts: 5% of eligible hosted accounts with a stratified sample across ARR bands and known streaming usage patterns
Metering implementation: emit separate counters (input_tokens, output_tokens, streaming_seconds) in the rate engine; apply treatment rules at billing generation stage to avoid heavy runtime changes
Telemetry: add cohort tags to usage and invoice events; create Grafana and Looker slices for quick evaluation
Legal/Contracts: update enterprise security questionnaire language to explain per-token definitions, retention windows for usage logs, and data access controls
Communication: in-product banner for cohort customers explaining pricing experiment and link to FAQ and support
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (now): finalize PRD, legal language, and engineering scope; gating review with Security and Billing (Week 0)
Phase 1 (Week 1-2): implement separate counters and billing-rule toggles in sandbox; run synthetic tests with recorded workloads
Phase 2 (Week 3-6): launch 5% cohort (T1 and T2 split) with active monitoring; weekly readouts
Phase 3 (Week 7-10): evaluate results vs success criteria; decide on broader rollout, parameter tuning, or rollback
Phase 4: update docs, pricing page, enterprise contract templates, and console billing UI if proceeding to GA
